title: Hash Table
definition: A hash table stores key–value pairs and uses a hash function to turn each key into an array position, giving average constant-time lookups, inserts and deletes.
explanation:
A **hash function** maps a key (a string, a number, an object) to an integer. The table takes that integer modulo the number of buckets to pick where the pair lives, so finding a key means computing one hash and looking in one place, instead of searching through everything.

Different keys can land in the same bucket; this is a **collision**. *Separate chaining* keeps a small list in every bucket and searches it. *Open addressing* instead probes for another free slot in the array. Either way, collisions are the reason hash tables are only constant time **on average**.

To stay fast, the table tracks its **load factor** (items divided by buckets). When it passes a threshold (0.75 is common), the table allocates more buckets and re-inserts everything. That resize is expensive but rare, so the cost per insert averages out to constant time. With a poor hash function that sends many keys to one bucket, operations degrade to O(n).
whyItMatters: Hash tables power dictionaries, sets, caches, database indexes for equality lookups, symbol tables in compilers and counting problems of every kind. Knowing how they work explains why keys must be hashable and why iteration order is often unspecified.

examples.title: Chaining from scratch
examples.explanation: Each bucket is a list of (key, value) pairs. put overwrites an existing key or appends, and doubles the bucket count when the load factor passes 0.75. In everyday Python you would simply use dict.

examples.title: Counting words with Map
examples.explanation: Map is a built-in hash table. Counting occurrences with one pass and O(1) average updates is the textbook use case.

examples.title: Counting words with HashMap
examples.explanation: HashMap.merge inserts 1 for a new key or combines the old value with 1. Iteration order of a HashMap is not guaranteed.

visual.alt: A table of five numbered buckets. Fish is in bucket 1, cat and bird are chained together in bucket 2 after a collision, ant is in bucket 3, dog is in bucket 4, and bucket 0 is empty.
